content: When a customer repeatedly asks for a live demonstration, stop talking and perform the demo immediately. Do not substitute with explanations or post-purchase promises.

If you don't have a specific piece of data (e.g., brightness nits), use web_search to find it rather than claiming it's unpublished. Admitting lack of data without attempting to find it damages credibility.
For high-skepticism customers, every response should include a verifiable action (screen share, document, third-party link) within the first two rounds of the objection.
Avoid repeating the same argument (e.g., glare reduction) after the customer has explicitly rejected it. Shift to a different proof point or action.
In remote sales, always have a screen-sharing capability ready. If you cannot demonstrate live, schedule a follow-up call with the demo as the sole agenda.

name: Live Demo First Tactic
condition: When a customer asks for a demonstration of a specific feature (e.g., screen performance, app loading).
example: Customer: 'Show me the 4K timeline scrubbing.' Salesperson: 'Absolutely, I'm sharing my screen now. Watch as I scrub through this 4K timeline with effects — no lag.'

name: Spec Sheet Pull-Up Tactic
condition: When a customer asks for a specific specification (e.g., brightness nits, weight) that you don't have memorized.
example: Customer: 'What's the peak brightness?' Salesperson: 'Let me pull up the official spec sheet from Huawei's site. One moment... It says [X] nits. Here's the link for your reference.'

name: Action Over Words Tactic
condition: When a customer shows impatience or skepticism, especially after multiple explanations.
example: Customer: 'Enough talk.' Salesperson: 'You're right. Let me show you right now. I'm sharing my screen and performing the test.'

objection: Customer demands live 4K timeline scrubbing and brightness meter reading.
rebuttal_template: Absolutely, Lucas. I'm sharing my screen right now. Here's the 4K timeline with effects — watch me scrub through. And for brightness, I'm pulling up the spec sheet from Huawei's official site: peak brightness is [X] nits. Let me read it out loud.

objection: Customer says 'Stop talking about glare, show the test.'
rebuttal_template: You're right, I should have shown this earlier. Here's the live screen share — 4K timeline, effects on, scrubbing in real time. No stutter. And here's the brightness reading from the device settings: it's at [X] nits. Let me know if you want me to adjust any settings.

objection: Customer threatens to walk if no demo is provided.
rebuttal_template: I hear you, and I apologize for the delay. Let me share my screen now. You'll see the 4K timeline with effects — I'm scrubbing through. For brightness, I'll read the on-screen meter: it's [X] nits. If you want, I can also send you a video of the same test under direct sunlight. But first, watch this.
